wild hare.line: A hare breaks from the bracken in one long grey streak.
wild hare.success: Clean and quick. The hare comes home as meat and hide, and nothing is wasted.
escapes: The hare turns once where the ground falls away and is gone before you can follow.
The hare doubles back through the bracken; by the time you read the track, it is cold.

grouse.line: The grouse erupts almost underfoot, wings hammering the quiet apart.
grouse.success: One sure shot through the trees. Meat and feathers come home.
escapes: The grouse is already behind three trunks before the bow is level.
A burst of wings, one falling feather, and empty air.

pheasant.line: Copper and green flash low between the hazels, bright enough to betray the bird.
pheasant.success: The pheasant drops cleanly. The long flight feathers are kept with the meat.
escapes: The pheasant climbs hard through a gap in the canopy and clears the wood.
You catch the colour a heartbeat too late; it is already over the hedge.

red deer.line: A red deer stands beyond the birches, listening with its whole body.
red deer.success: A hard hunt, ended cleanly. Venison, hide, and what the antlers give come home.
escapes: The deer catches the wind, bounds once, and the whole herd pours away behind it.
One branch snaps under your heel. The deer is gone before the sound finishes.

wild boar.line: The boar works the roots under an oak, black-backed and heavier than it first looked.
wild boar.success: The boar is brought down cleanly. Meat, hide, and tusk are carried out together.
escapes: The boar crashes straight through cover too dense to follow and keeps going.
It wheels at the last instant and vanishes down an old run under the holly.
